title: A signed-in navigation to / from a link with utm_* records link.visited once per person, source and half hour; a fetch, a repeat, a signed-out visit and a view-as record none
steps: S1: signed in as ceo@tracy.ai, GET /?utm_source=tracy&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=tracy-beta-2026-10&utm_content=followup-d with Accept text/html twice, once with Accept application/json, then GET / with no utm_*.
S2: the same link with no session cookie.
S3: move the clock one ENTERED_WINDOW_MS and open the link signed in again.
S4: open /?utm_source=tracy&utm_medium=email as an admin viewing customer@example.com (tracy_view cookie, view-as on).
expect: S1: exactly one link.visited row whose data is {email: ceo@tracy.ai, source: tracy, medium: email, campaign: tracy-beta-2026-10, content: followup-d}.
S2: 302 to /login?utm_source=tracy... and no new link.visited row.
S3: a second link.visited row; linkVisitKey ignores the case of the address and is the same within one half hour.
evidence: Lifecycle mails of 2026-11-02 to 87 existing customers left no click record: a signed-in browser opening /?utm_... never reaches /login, so login.visited saw none of them
fence: Usage never stands in the way: the redirect is unchanged and the signal is never awaited; only an HTML navigation from a real session counts, so link scanners (no cookie), fetches and an admin's view-as add no rows

tests: workspaceRoutes: a signed-in navigation to / with utm_* records link.visited once per half hour
workspaceRoutes: a view as a customer records no link.visited for the customer
